entries.name: Noisy rectifier
entries.definition: A stochastic activation that adds zero-mean noise to a preactivation and then applies the positive-part rectifier, producing h=max(0,a+z).
entries.identity_notes: This record covers the noisy rectifier described in Bengio et al. Section 2.1, with standard logistic noise as the analytically characterized special case. It is a stochastic activation, distinct from deterministic ReLU or softplus, input-only corruption, weight-noise dense layers and multiplicative dropout. The paper credits earlier rectifier work; this record does not claim that the 2013 paper invented noisy rectification. limitations: Equality of the logistic-noise mean to softplus does not make a sampled noisy rectifier a deterministic softplus unit. Passing the mean through a nonlinear downstream loss does not generally preserve the expected loss.

The standard logistic activation and mean formulas change with the noise distribution or scale. Gaussian noise is mentioned as a practical alternative, but it does not inherit the displayed logistic identities.

Occasional activation permits gradient flow for some samples but does not guarantee that inactive units recover promptly, that every derivative-through-expectation interchange is valid, or that conditional computation saves wall-clock time.
No empirical speed, accuracy or sparsity advantage is asserted. The original authors’ implementation and later noisy-activation variants were not audited.

claims.statement: For a preactivation a, sample zero-mean additive noise z and output max(0,a+z). With the source’s standard logistic density sigma(z)*(1-sigma(z)), the probability of a positive output is sigma(a), and the conditional mean output is log(1+exp(a)). These identities are specific to that logistic-noise choice, not arbitrary zero-mean noise. Holding a sampled noise value fixed, the derivative with respect to a is 1 on the positive side and 0 on the negative side, with a nondifferentiable boundary at a+z=0. Noise can occasionally turn an otherwise inactive unit on or an active unit off. The source also suggests adjusting a unit bias when a moving activity rate falls below a chosen target; that heuristic is additional to the forward activation rule.

entries.name: Stochastic-times-smooth unit
entries.definition: A stochastic activation that sets p=sigmoid(a), samples a Bernoulli gate with success probability sqrt(p), and outputs the gate multiplied by sqrt(p).

The Bernoulli gate and nonzero amplitude are both sqrt(p); it is neither an ordinary Bernoulli(p) output nor fixed-rate dropout. The source’s Figure 2 uses the reversed wording Smooth Times Stoch. for this experimental unit family. The identity is not the generic straight-through estimator or stochastic depth. claims.statement: Compute p=sigmoid(a), draw b in {0,1} with P(b=1)=sqrt(p), and return h=b*sqrt(p). Conditional on a, E[h]=p, P(h>0)=sqrt(p), and the nonzero output is sqrt(p). Backpropagation through the smooth multiplier can hold the discrete gate fixed. This path does not include the derivative of the gate’s probability law: as a curator consequence of the displayed rule, its expected derivative for the loss h is p-prime/2, while d E[h]/d a=p-prime. Proposition 2 gives an asymptotic relationship E[f(h)]=f(p)+o(sqrt(p)) as p tends to zero for the stated differentiable-function setting; it does not state equality at a finite activation probability.

entries.name: Black box variational inference
entries.definition: A variational-inference procedure that estimates evidence-lower-bound gradients from samples of a tractable variational distribution using its score function and model log joint, with mean-field local signals and score control variates to manage estimator variance.
entries.identity_notes: This record covers Ranganath, Gerrish and Blei’s original BBVI Algorithms 1–2 and their score-function estimator, mean-field local signals and control variates. It is not every black-box inference method, a pathwise reparameterization estimator, a model architecture or an amortized recognition network such as NVIL. The hierarchical data-subsampling extension is outside the validated mechanism scope here. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 337 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 22 and 22 lines respectively. All 15 unique matched line contents were inspected in full: the preceding gradient-estimator records, their cited Bengio source, saved source-reading scopes, reviews and open discovery leads, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Thirteen exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and six full native neighboring records were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Black box still requires sampling from and evaluating the variational distribution, score derivatives with respect to its parameters, and evaluation of the model log joint at sampled latent states. The method does not require differentiation through a discrete latent sample, but support and integrability conditions remain necessary.

Raw unbiasedness requires the regularity assumptions behind differentiation under the expectation and zero expected score. A model normalization constant independent of lambda cancels from this gradient; a parameter-dependent term cannot be discarded on that basis.

A coefficient fixed independently of the gradient samples preserves expectation when the relevant moments exist. A coefficient estimated from those same samples can correlate with the sample score and introduce bias. The paper reports separate sample counts for coefficient estimation and gradient calculation, but the inspected description does not establish an exact sampling-independence convention; no implementation behavior is asserted.

Population-optimal control-variate scaling and conditional-expectation variance reduction do not guarantee that estimated coefficients or every additional removal of zero-mean terms reduces finite-sample variance. Zero or poorly estimated score variance requires handling beyond division by the displayed ratio.

The practical step schedule and change-in-parameters stopping rule do not establish global optimality or exact posterior recovery. Mean-field factorization can limit the approximation. The printed hierarchical subsampling formulas need a separate weighting audit and are not curated as a verified extension here.
No benchmark result, author-code run, general convergence proof or posterior-quality certification is included.

claims.statement: For fixed observed x and joint model p(x,z), choose a variational family q(z;lambda), sample z from q, and maximize L(lambda)=E_q[log p(x,z)-log q(z;lambda)] by stochastic ascent. Under the normalized-score and differentiation-under-expectation conditions, the raw gradient is E_q[grad_lambda log q(z;lambda)*(log p(x,z)-log q(z;lambda))], estimated by a Monte Carlo average. The mean-field version factors q into q_i(z_i;lambda_i) and uses for each factor the model log terms that depend on z_i together with -log q_i; unrelated terms cancel in expectation under the stated factorization. For parameter coordinate d in factor i, let h_d be the score and f_d be that score times the local log signal. A fixed control-variate coefficient gives f_d-a_d*h_d because E[h_d]=0; the population variance-minimizing coefficient is Cov(f_d,h_d)/Var(h_d) when these quantities exist and Var(h_d)>0. The source estimates coefficients from samples and averages corrected contributions before a stochastic-ascent update. Its fixed-coefficient expectation identity does not by itself justify arbitrary reuse of samples to estimate both the coefficient and corrected gradient.

claims.statement: Draw independent Gumbel noise and compute y=softmax((log(alpha)+G)/tau) with positive finite weights and tau>0. claims.statement: Let P_theta(x,h) be the generative joint model and Q_phi(h|x) an inference-network distribution that can be sampled and evaluated efficiently. For each observed x, maximize the bound E_Q[log P_theta(x,h)-log Q_phi(h|x)]. Draw latent samples from Q. The raw model-gradient estimator averages d log P_theta(x,h)/d theta; the raw inference-gradient estimator averages the learning signal l=log P_theta(x,h)-log Q_phi(h|x) times d log Q_phi(h|x)/d phi. Its score expectation is zero, so baselines independent of the current latent sample conditional on x can be subtracted without changing the raw gradient expectation. The method fits an input-dependent neural baseline and maintains a scalar running center. It also divides the centered signal by max(1,sqrt(v)), where v is a running variance estimate, to adapt the update scale. In the supplement’s concrete minibatch ordering, subtract the input baseline, compute batch signal mean and variance, update the running center and variance using those batch statistics, then form centered/scaled inference updates and baseline updates; the model gradient remains unweighted by this signal. For layered factorizations, local learning signals omit terms that are independent of the relevant sampled descendants under the conditional score expectation, with separate baselines and variance estimates.

native_neighbors.name: REINFORCE
native_neighbors.definition: A family of stochastic reinforcement-learning update rules that multiply a sampled reward relative to an admissible baseline by the derivative of the log probability of the sampled action or unit output, with a nonnegative learning-rate factor.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record covers Williams’s REINFORCE update family, including its basic immediate-reward rule and the stated fixed-episode extension. The characteristic eligibility is a score-function derivative. This is not the entire reinforcement-learning task, an action-value bootstrapping rule, PPO’s clipped surrogate, a generic optimizer, or every estimator that uses random perturbations. The acronym names the update structure; no trained policy instance is represented. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 334 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 66 and 66 lines respectively. Match-centered excerpts from all 41 unique hit contents were inspected: ordinary verb reinforce in existing ant/search/pseudo-label records and calculations, plus neighboring Gumbel straight-through discussions and the new gradient-estimator discovery lead, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Ten exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and six full native neighboring records were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The score identity requires valid differentiable probabilities or densities and conditions permitting differentiation of the expectation. Parameter-dependent support or extra direct reward dependence requires additional analysis; a discrete black-box reward need not itself have a derivative with respect to the action.

A baseline that depends on the same sampled action or its current reward does not automatically preserve the unbiased score identity. An input-dependent baseline or a statistic based on past trials can satisfy the stated conditional-independence requirement.
Baseline choice changes variance and can increase it. The mean reward is not generally the minimum-variance baseline, and low variance is not guaranteed simply by naming a baseline.

Expected gradient alignment is not monotonic improvement of each sampled update, a global optimum guarantee, or a convergence theorem for arbitrary step sizes. Zero coordinate rates can prevent movement even at a nonzero gradient.

The original episodic construction assumes a declared finite episode and parameters fixed throughout it. It is not a blanket justification for arbitrary online bootstrapping, truncation, discounting, off-policy sample reuse or action-dependent baselines.

The primary journal paper was read through a public third-party copy and checked against publisher metadata. Only the declared method pages were inspected; its full proof appendix and empirical literature were not independently audited.

definition_evidence.locator: Sections 2–4, PDF pp.2–8 / journal pp.230–236, especially Theorem 1 and Equations (5)–(10); Section 5, PDF pp.8–9 / journal pp.236–237, Equation (11) and Theorem 2

claims.statement: For a stochastic unit with conditional mass or density g_i(y_i;w_i,x_i), sample its output y_i, receive scalar reinforcement r and update weight w_ij by alpha_ij*(r-b_ij)*d log(g_i)/d w_ij. The baseline b_ij is conditionally independent of the current unit output given the weights and unit inputs; it may depend on permitted input context or past experience. In the original immediate-reward formulation, the nonnegative rate factor may depend at most on the unit’s parameter vector and trial index; it is not chosen from the current sampled output. Under the stated differentiability and environmental assumptions, the baseline-centered score product estimates the corresponding expected-reward gradient component. A common scalar rate gives an expected update proportional to that gradient; differing nonnegative coordinate rates generally rescale its components and need not preserve collinearity. For a Bernoulli-logistic unit with probability p and input x_j, the eligibility is (y-p)*x_j. In the fixed-length episodic extension, hold parameters fixed during the episode, sum each parameter’s score eligibilities over time, and multiply that sum by terminal reward minus an admissible episode baseline when updating at the end.

native_neighbors.name: Stochastic depth
native_neighbors.definition: A residual-network training procedure that randomly bypasses residual transformations during training and uses all residual transformations with survival-probability scaling during inference.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record covers the original 2016 stochastic-depth procedure with a block-survival draw per minibatch and test-time residual scaling. It is a training procedure for residual networks, not the residual architecture itself. Modern per-example drop-path functions, inverted scaling conventions and learned dynamic-depth methods require separate version assessment. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 276 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 5 and 5 lines respectively. Every text hit was a prior candidate lead or a closely related variant lead. Nine exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and three native neighboring mechanisms were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Identity bypass is conditional on the skip path and activation: a post-addition ReLU clips negative skip values, and a dimension-changing projection is not the same operation as an identity map. The procedure cannot be transferred to an arbitrary incompatible block by merely deleting its output.

The survival schedule in the core method varies with network depth, not automatically with elapsed training time. The paper’s final-block probability of0.5 is an experimental choice. Mini-batch sampling and inference scaling differ from later per-example or inverted-scaled implementations.

Survival-weighted inference is a practical combination of shared-weight subnetworks, not generally the exact expected prediction of the stochastic nonlinear network. Reduced expected active-block count does not by itself guarantee a proportional wall-clock saving; computation must actually be bypassed.

The source’s empirical gradient and benchmark observations do not certify absence of vanishing gradients, universal regularization improvement or arbitrarily deep trainability. No author code or trained network was executed.

definition_evidence.locator: Section3 and Equations2–5, PDF pp.4–7; residual skip definition Section2, PDFp.3; conclusion PDF pp.13–14

claims.statement: Assign each residual block a survival probability and, for each training minibatch, sample whether to execute its residual transformation. An active block adds its residual output to the skip path before the architecture’s output activation; an inactive block bypasses the residual transformation while preserving the skip path. The source’s identity reduction relies on its nonnegative activations and compatible skip connection. It proposes a linear decrease in survival probability with block depth from an always-present input to a chosen last-block probability, while also considering a uniform assignment. The expected number of active residual blocks is the sum of their survival probabilities. During inference, activate every residual transformation and multiply its output by its training survival probability before adding the skip path. The original convention does not divide active training residuals by the survival probability.
